name: kero
description: A cross-platform native terminal app optimized for agents
readmeExcerpt:
# Kero

A terminal for coding agents, on macOS, Windows and Linux.

Run Claude Code, Codex, a dev server or a test watcher each in its own session. Kero groups sessions by project in a sidebar that shows which are working, which need you and which are done.

- **Sessions outlive the window.** They run in `kerod`, a small daemon, so quitting Kero leaves them running. Reopen it and every pane and its scrollback is back.
- **Status at a glance.** Each pane is working, waiting, idle, error or exited. <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>J</kbd> jumps to the one that needs you, and Kero notifies you when an agent finishes, fails or is blocked.
- **A CLI agents can drive.** `kero` starts sessions, splits panes, types into them, waits on them and reads their screens.
- **Remote hosts.** Run agents on a Linux box, a cloud VM, a Mac, a Windows PC or WSL and see them in the same sidebar, over SSH or Tailscale. They keep running when your laptop sleeps. See [Remote Hosts](docs/remote.md).
- **Ghostty under the hood.** Terminals render with libghostty, so Ghostty themes, fonts and config keys just work.

## Install

Download Kero from the [releases page](https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases), then choose **Kero › Install Command Line Tool…** to put `kero` on your `PATH`.

```sh
kero new -n fix-login -- claude
```

To run sessions on a Linux server, a Mac or a Windows PC, install the server build there, then add the machine in **Settings › Hosts**:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases/latest/download/install-server.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases/latest/download/install-server.ps1 | iex
```

See the [docs](docs/index.md) for more.

## Prior art

- [**Rex**](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/installation): Mitchell Hashimoto's terminal and multiplexer in one native app, with sessions that persist through a server and a scriptable CLI.
- [**Herdr**](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr): a terminal multiplexer for running many coding agents in one terminal, with agent status detection.

## License

MIT

aiSummary.oneLiner: A native, Swift-based macOS terminal workspace optimized for managing isolated, persistent AI coding agent sessions.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Kero is a terminal application built specifically for macOS using Swift. It leverages the libghostty engine for high-performance rendering. The terminal is designed to manage multiple AI coding agents, such as Claude Code or Codex, in isolated sessions. These sessions are persistent, running in a background daemon, which means you can close the terminal without interrupting the agents. It organizes these sessions by project, providing a unified workspace for AI-assisted development.
keyFeatures: Daemon architecture: Sessions run in a background daemon, ensuring they outlive the terminal window.
Native performance: The application is built natively in Swift using the high-performance libghostty rendering engine.
Project grouping: The interface organizes sessions by project in a convenient sidebar.
Status visualization: Each pane clearly displays its current state, such as working, waiting, or idle.
Agent isolation: Users can run multiple agents like Claude Code or Codex in completely independent environments.

useCases.title: Long-running tasks
useCases.description: Run development servers or test watchers without worrying about accidentally closing the terminal.

useCases.title: Agent management
useCases.description: Manage multiple AI coding assistants simultaneously in distinct, organized sessions.

useCases.title: Background processing
useCases.description: Execute complex compilations or data processing scripts that continue running in the background.

useCases.title: Project context switching
useCases.description: Switch between different project environments quickly using the sidebar grouping feature.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: It is tailored for macOS developers working directly with large language models in their local environments. System administrators running multiple persistent tasks across sessions will also benefit from its architecture.
